message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day battles of the Napoleonic Wars.  Casualty estimates vary depending on the source and how “casualties” are defined (killed, wounded, missing, captured).  A commonly cited figure is:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| **French** | ~25 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |
| **Allied (British, Dutch‑German, Prussian)** | ~22 000 (killed, wounded, missing) |

These totals include both killed and wounded; some historians separate them into:

* **French** – 8 000–9 000 killed, 12 000–13 000 wounded, 2 000–3 000 missing/captured  
* **Allied** – 7 000–8 000 killed, 10 000–11 000 wounded, 3 000–4 000 missing/captured  

Because battlefield reporting was chaotic and many wounded later died from disease or were not counted, the numbers can differ by a few thousand.  For a more detailed breakdown you can consult primary reports such as the French *Journal de l’Armée* or the British *Official Correspondence of the War Office*.
